name: MAX3232ESE+T
title: MAX3222/MAX3232/MAX3237/MAX3241: 3.0V to 5.5V RS-232 transceivers with four 0.1µF charge-pump capacitors
summary: A family of RS-232 transceivers that run from a single 3.0V to 5.5V supply: two regulated charge pumps with four small external capacitors makes ±5.5V rails, so the drivers swing at least ±5V into 3kΩ. MAX3232 has two drivers and two receivers and no shutdown; MAX3222 adds a 1µA shutdown and a receiver enable. MAX3237 (5 drivers, 3 receivers) reaches 1Mbps in MegaBaud mode, and MAX3241 (3 drivers, 5 receivers) forms a whole serial port able to power a mouse; both have shutdown and always-on complementary receiver outputs. MAX3232ESE+ is the -40°C to +85°C MAX3232 in the 16-pin narrow SO.

notes: + marks a lead-free package.
*Dice are tested at TA = +25°C, DC parameters only.
MAX3237CAI+: 16 SSOP should read 28 SSOP.
MAX3237EAI+: 0°C to +70°C should read -40°C to +85°C.

circuits.title: MAX3222 typical operating circuit
circuits.description: Two-driver, two-receiver RS-232 port on a 3.3V rail. C1 and C2 are the flying capacitors of the doubling and inverting charge pumps, C3 and C4 hold the V+ and V- rails, and C5 decouples VCC. Logic signals on T1IN and T2IN leave inverted at RS-232 levels on T1OUT and T2OUT; line signals on R1IN and R2IN come back inverted at logic levels on R1OUT and R2OUT. EN gates the receiver outputs and SHDN switches the charge pump and drivers off.

parts.note: V+ reservoir; may return to VCC or to ground
V- reservoir, positive end at ground

notes: Pin numbers are those of the 18-pin DIP/SO package.
Every receiver input has its 5kΩ load to ground inside the chip.
C1 to C4 follow Table 2 at other supply voltages.

circuits.title: MAX3232 typical operating circuit
circuits.description: The same two-in, two-out RS-232 port with the MAX3232, which has neither shutdown nor enable. Four 0.1µF capacitors run the charge pump (C1, C2 flying; C3, C4 on V+ and V-) and C5 decouples the 3.3V supply. Each driver inverts its logic input onto an RS-232 line; each receiver inverts its line back to a logic output.

parts.note: V+ reservoir; may return to VCC or to ground
V- reservoir, positive end at ground

notes: Every receiver input has its 5kΩ load to ground inside the chip.
C1 to C4 follow Table 2 at other supply voltages.

circuits.title: MAX3237 typical operating circuit
circuits.description: Five drivers and three receivers for a fast modem link. All four charge-pump capacitors and the supply bypass are 0.1µF; C3 on V+ is returned to VCC. R1OUTB repeats receiver 1 without inversion and keeps working when EN or SHDN turn the rest off, so line activity can still be seen. MBAUD picks the normal or the 1Mbps transmit rate.

circuits.title: MAX3241 typical operating circuit
circuits.description: A full serial port, three drivers and five receivers, from 3.3V. The charge pump uses four 0.1µF capacitors and VCC has a 0.1µF bypass. R1OUTB and R2OUTB give non-inverted copies of receivers 1 and 2 that stay active in shutdown and with EN high, for watching a ring-indicate or similar line while the host is asleep.

T1IN and T2IN are grounded so T1OUT and T2OUT sit at the positive RS-232 level, and T3IN is tied to VCC so T3OUT sits at the negative level; those three outputs feed the mouse supply lines of the computer serial port, and the mouse data comes back on a receiver input. operation.text: Two on-chip charge pumps make the driver rails: one doubles to +5.5V on V+, the other inverts to -5.5V on V-, and both hold those levels for any VCC from 3.0V to 5.5V. They run in bursts, switching on when a rail falls below 5.5V and off once it is above. Each pump needs a flying capacitor (C1 for V+, C2 for V-) and a reservoir capacitor (C3 on V+, C4 on V-).

Each transmitter inverts a CMOS logic input into a 5.0V EIA/TIA-232 level. MAX3222, MAX3232 and MAX3241 are guaranteed to 120kbps into 3kΩ in parallel with 1000pF and typically reach 235kbps. Outputs may be paralleled to drive several receivers or a mouse. In shutdown the MAX3222, MAX3237 and MAX3241 outputs go high impedance, and with power removed all four parts let their outputs be driven to ±12V. The inputs have no pull-ups; unused inputs go to GND or VCC.

With MBAUD at GND the MAX3237 transmitters are guaranteed to 250kbps into 3kΩ in parallel with 1000pF. With MBAUD at VCC they are guaranteed to 1Mbps into 3kΩ in parallel with 250pF for VCC between 3.0V and 4.5V, and into 3kΩ in parallel with 1000pF on a 5V ±10% supply.

Each receiver turns an RS-232 level into an inverted CMOS logic output. On the MAX3222, MAX3237 and MAX3241 those outputs are three-state, and whether they run in shutdown follows Table 1. The non-inverting B outputs (R1OUTB on the MAX3237; R1OUTB and R2OUTB on the MAX3241) are active whatever EN and SHDN say. A host whose UART is unpowered can therefore have the main receiver outputs off, so no current flows into the UART's protection diodes, and still detect a ring-indicate or other line activity through the B outputs.

Pulling SHDN low cuts supply current below 1µA: the charge pumps stop, V+ falls to VCC, V- is pulled to 0V and every transmitter output turns off to high impedance. Leaving shutdown takes about 100µs. Tie SHDN to VCC when shutdown is not wanted. Receiver outputs, both kinds, ignore SHDN.
With EN high, each R_OUT output floats (high impedance); EN low turns them on. R1OUTB and R2OUTB stay active either way, and EN does not affect the transmitter outputs.

C1 to C4 may be polarized or not; their type matters little. At 3.3V each is 0.1µF; Table 2 gives the least values for other supplies, and smaller values are not allowed. Doubling the values lowers transmitter-output ripple and trims power a little. C2, C3 and C4 may grow alone, but C1 may only grow together with them so the ratio of C1 to the rest holds. At the minimum values, pick capacitors whose value does not drop much over temperature, or use a larger nominal value. ESR, which tends to rise when cold, adds to the ripple on both pump rails.
A 0.1µF bypass on VCC is enough in most designs. Where supply noise matters, use a bypass equal to C1. Bypass capacitors go as close to the chip as possible.
At supplies as low as 2.7V the transmitter outputs still reach the ±3.7V levels of EIA/TIA-562.

On leaving shutdown or at power-up, with each transmitter loaded by 3kΩ in parallel with 2500pF, the outputs move to their RS-232 levels without ringing or glitches. The transmitters switch on only once V- exceeds about 3V in magnitude.

The MAX3241 is built to power a serial mouse from a low supply. It was tried with mice from major makers and met each one's current and voltage needs. Figure 4a gives output voltage against load current at VCC = 3.0V, and Figure 4b the connection.

MAX3222, MAX3232 and MAX3241 keep at least ±5.0V at their transmitter outputs at high data rates: at 120kbps with every transmitter switching into an RS-232 load shunted by 1000pF, and at 235kbps with one transmitter switching while each output sees a receiver load plus 1000pF. The MAX3237 keeps ±5.0V up to 1Mbps with MBAUD = VCC when each output sees a receiver load plus 250pF.
The parts connect directly to 5V logic families such as ACT and HCT CMOS; Table 3 lists which supply combinations work with which logic families.
